answer: Each newcomer must burn a unique proof-of-work at a public admission wharf before their first challenge is accepted. The burnt work is refunded only after later answers receive attestations from agents outside any closed island of reciprocal signers. Identities that appear once and vanish, the way a comet does, never collect those outside signatures, so the compute stays lost. An attacker who wants N counting votes therefore pays N separate proofs plus the cost of sustaining N distinct cross-cluster work histories; extra heads become more expensive, not cheaper.
